scope: First member-initiated native ingress: the native host issues a MemberExecution channel + worker credential when it prepares a dispatch, delivers the credential only to the confirmed pane process environment, and accepts one canonical report action (member_report) when the real socket peer is that process or its descendant, the credential/channel/execution/member match, the execution is running, and the live grant includes member_report. This is NOT full member execution: no task completion, no terminal control, no AgentCli prompt/wait, no pane-output redaction, no stop/pause/resume, no cross-backend inheritance, default entry, packaging, install or UI acceptance.
existing_capability_and_gap: Reused Core TaskRegistry::prepare_member_dispatch/confirm_launch/LaunchSpec, AuthorityEngine::issue_worker_credential/revoke_worker_credential/check_bound_worker_action, ChannelRegistry, canonical events, redaction::Redactor, and herdr's real pane PTY. The gap was that a spawned member process had no host-issued identity and no ingress at all; the owner gate refused native starts whenever any active worker credential existed.
behavior: prepare_execution issues a MemberExecution channel and a worker credential bound to the new execution/member and returns them only through the child environment (VIVA_MEMBER_CHANNEL, VIVA_MEMBER_CREDENTIAL). The member CLI `viva runtime member report --status <progress|blocked|failed|done> [--detail <text>]` connects to the native socket and sends viva.member.report. The handler captures the real accepted-socket PID/UID, requires the peer UID to match the host, requires the peer PID to be the confirmed execution PID or a descendant (process lineage), re-verifies the confirmed OS start marker, then calls check_bound_worker_action with action member_report and the dispatch grant. On success it appends native_member_reported with execution/task/member/grant/channel/status and a credential-redacted detail. Refusals append native_member_report_refused with fixed reason markers and never the credential, detail or request body. The credential and channel are revoked on process exit and on failed start. The owner gate now accepts active credentials only for executions this host owns; foreign active credentials still refuse the host.

negative_fixtures: No credential; a valid credential used by an unrelated process (lineage refusal); a grant without the member_report action; a revoked credential after execution exit; a foreign active worker credential at host startup. All refusals are audited with fixed markers and no credential/detail/argv. The member client never accepts a credential on argv and never auto-starts a legacy server.
boundaries: The credential is a bearer secret delivered through the process environment; same-UID processes can read it and process lineage is not an OS sandbox. Do not claim general worker isolation.
Only one member effect exists (progress/blocked/failed/done report). It never completes a task, never changes task status, and never writes task_results.
Detail redaction covers only the worker credential itself; general native output/persistence redaction and pane history remain disabled.
Process lineage and start-marker checks are implemented on macOS with libproc and on Linux via /proc; Linux is not executed by this evidence.
Native host restart leaves DB requested/running executions and active credentials unowned, so the preview still fails closed; no reconciliation.

ci_race_fix: CI run 42838411136 exposed a fast-exit race in the #198 owner-gate fixture: the start marker was read after the LaunchSpec write, so a zero-lifetime /bin/sh -c "exit 0" could be reaped before the read. The marker is now read first inside execution_started, and the fixture uses sleep 0.2 instead of exit 0. A process already gone before the marker is readable still fails confirmation honestly and remains unresolved.
